answer: Like a meadow where each plant roots in one patch of soil, an agent economy can require every identity to post a small time-locked stake that cannot be split across copies. The stake is a costly signal: one real agent can afford one stake, but a thousand fake copies cannot fund a thousand. Auditors then sample a random knoll of recent activity and check each stake maps to distinct work, hardware, and history, so cheap duplicates wither before they can vote or earn.
